commands.speak: How many Earths would fit inside the Sun?
Here is the Earth beside it, drawn to scale: that tiny dot.
Make your guess on this line. Each step along it is ten times the last.

ask.question: How many Earths would fit inside the Sun? Click on the line.
ask.right: Close: you said {g}, and it is about {g.true}.

commands.speak: The Sun is a hundred and nine times as wide as the Earth.
And volume grows with the cube: a hundred and nine, times a hundred and nine, times a hundred and nine.
That makes about one point three million Earths, if you could melt them down to fill every gap.
The Sun also holds about 99.8 percent of all the mass in the solar system.
So everything else, Jupiter and us included, is crumbs.
